label: Provided the doctrine of disinterested divine love central to Ihya Ulum al-Din
description: Al-Ghazali explicitly cited Rabi'a al-Adawiyya at length in the Book of Love (Kitab al-Mahabba) of his Ihya Ulum al-Din, adopting her distinction between mercenary devotion for reward and pure love of God's essence.
dialecticalTension: Elevates affective purity of intention (ikhlas) above legalistic moral calculation.
historicalContext: Transmitted from 8th-century Basra into 11th-century Sunni Sufi synthesis.

citations.author: Al-Ghazali
citations.work: Ihya Ulum al-Din (The Book of Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment)

label: Revered as foundational Sufi authority on ontological love (mahabba)
description: Ibn Arabi honored Rabi'a in al-Futuhat al-Makkiyya as an unsurpassed exemplar of divine love and spiritual station, weaving her mahabba ethics into his metaphysics of the Unity of Being.
dialecticalTension: Unites passionate devotional love with cosmic ontological unity.
historicalContext: Foundational Sufi canon from Basra to Andalusia.

citations.author: Margaret Smith
citations.work: Rabi'a the Mystic & Her Fellow-Saints in Islam

label: Originated the philosophical ethics of unconditional disinterested divine love
description: Rabi'a formulated the doctrine that true devotion loves the Divine solely for divine beauty and majesty, rejecting both fear of Hellfire and desire for Paradise.
dialecticalTension: Transforms ethics from transactional salvation into pure non-instrumental love.
